ARABIC LANGUAGE — PREMIUM REVISION PAPER #16
====

GRADE: Grade 4
SUBJECT: ARABIC LANGUAGE
TIME ALLOWED: 120 minutes
TOTAL MARKS: 100
ASSESSMENT: CBC school-based practice paper

INSTRUCTIONS
----
1. Answer all questions.
2. For calculations, show your working and write the units.
3. For multiple choice, choose the one best answer.
4. Check your work before you hand in.

SECTION A — MULTIPLE CHOICE
----
1. Which Arabic word means "I"? (1 mark)
   A. شُكْرًا
   B. مَا اسْمُكَ؟
   C. مَرْحَبًا
   D. أَنَا

2. What does the phrase al-hamdu lillaah express? (1 mark)
   A. A request to sit down
   B. A question about a name
   C. Thanks to God
   D. A goodbye

3. Which sentence gives your own name? (1 mark)
   A. ismii Ahmad
   B. maa ismuka?
   C. kayfa haaluka?
   D. maʿa s-salaama

4. Which Arabic sentence means "I have a brother and a sister." (1 mark)
   A. هَذَا أَبِي
   B. عِنْدِي أَخٌ وَأُخْتٌ
   C. هَذِهِ أُمِّي
   D. أَبِي يَعْمَلُ

5. The nuclear family is made of (1 mark)
   A. grandparents and cousins
   B. neighbours
   C. parents and their children
   D. uncles and aunts only

6. What does the Arabic word فَوْقَ (fawqa) mean? (1 mark)
   A. beside
   B. at (near, by)
   C. above
   D. under

7. Which day begins the week in the Arabic list? (1 mark)
   A. al-khamiis
   B. al-ahad
   C. al-jumuʿa
   D. as-sabt

8. Which Arabic instruction means 'sit down'? (1 mark)
   A. ijlis
   B. iqraʾ
   C. qif
   D. ukhruj

9. What does the Arabic word طَعَامٌ (taʿaam) mean? (1 mark)
   A. food
   B. birthday
   C. friend
   D. please, go ahead

10. Which Arabic sentence means "I eat bread." (1 mark)
   A. أُحِبُّ الْمَوْزَ
   B. أَشْرَبُ الْمَاءَ
   C. آكُلُ الْخُبْزَ
   D. أُحِبُّ الْعَصِيرَ

11. How is the Arabic word سَمَكٌ read aloud in English letters? (1 mark)
   A. maa'
   B. milh
   C. bayd
   D. samak

12. How is the Arabic word أُذُنٌ read aloud in English letters? (1 mark)
   A. jism
   B. lisaan
   C. shaʿr
   D. udhun

13. What does the Arabic sentence كَيْفَ الْجَوُّ الْيَوْمَ؟ mean? (1 mark)
   A. The weather is rainy.
   B. The weather is hot.
   C. How is the weather today?
   D. The weather is cold.

14. How is the Arabic word زَهْرَةٌ read aloud in English letters? (1 mark)
   A. zahra
   B. nadhiif
   C. haarr
   D. sahaab

15. What happens to the voice at the end of a statement? (1 mark)
   A. It falls
   B. It rises
   C. It shouts
   D. It stops

16. What does the mark sukuun (a small circle) show? (1 mark)
   A. The letter has no vowel
   B. The letter is doubled
   C. The vowel is long
   D. The letter is silent and not written

17. How many letters are in the Arabic alphabet? (1 mark)
   A. 30
   B. 28
   C. 24
   D. 26

18. How do you read the syllable تِ? (1 mark)
   A. ti
   B. laa
   C. si
   D. nii

19. How do you read the syllable مُو? (1 mark)
   A. muu
   B. ja
   C. bu
   D. ta

20. How do you read the syllable بُ? (1 mark)
   A. du
   B. laa
   C. bu
   D. thaa

21. Which letter begins the word taawila? (1 mark)
   A. taa, the light ت
   B. thaa, ث
   C. Taa, the heavy ط
   D. daal, د

22. Which day is al-khamiis? (1 mark)
   A. Tuesday
   B. Saturday
   C. Friday
   D. Thursday

23. Which Arabic word means "Saturday"? (1 mark)
   A. الْيَوْمَ
   B. الْجُمُعَةُ
   C. السَّبْتُ
   D. الْأَرْبِعَاءُ

24. Which Arabic word means "school"? (1 mark)
   A. الْأَحَدُ
   B. أُسْبُوعٌ
   C. مَدْرَسَةٌ
   D. الثُّلَاثَاءُ

25. How is the Arabic word عَصِيرٌ read aloud in English letters? (1 mark)
   A. ʿasiir
   B. shamʿa
   C. ʿiid miilaad
   D. taʿaam

26. Which Arabic word means "delicious"? (1 mark)
   A. يَوْمٌ
   B. بِجَانِبِ
   C. لَذِيذٌ
   D. كَعْكَةٌ

27. Which Arabic word means "cold"? (1 mark)
   A. سَحَابٌ
   B. رِيحٌ
   C. بَارِدٌ
   D. حَارٌّ

28. What does the Arabic sentence وَالْمَطَرُ مِنَ السَّمَاءِ mean? (1 mark)
   A. I go to school on Monday.
   B. And the rain is from the sky.
   C. How beautiful the environment is!
   D. The sun is in the sky.

29. Which letter completes the word _ُور to make nuur (light)? (1 mark)
   A. ن (nuun)
   B. ب (baa)
   C. ت (taa)
   D. ي (yaa)

30. What is the name of the Arabic letter ح? (1 mark)
   A. Haa
   B. nuun
   C. Saad
   D. miim

31. What does the Arabic word خِزَانَةٌ (khizaana) mean? (1 mark)
   A. pen
   B. cupboard
   C. book
   D. bed

32. What does the Arabic sentence الْأَصْدِقَاءُ يَأْكُلُونَ الْكَعْكَةَ mean? (1 mark)
   A. I have a gift.
   B. I like the party.
   C. The friends eat the cake.
   D. My mother cooks the food.

33. What does the Arabic sentence نَحْنُ نَرْقُصُ mean? (1 mark)
   A. My mother cooks the food.
   B. I like the party.
   C. I have a gift.
   D. We dance.

34. Which Arabic word means "milk"? (1 mark)
   A. حَلِيبٌ
   B. مَوْزٌ
   C. مَاءٌ
   D. جَزَرٌ

35. Which Arabic sentence means "I eat rice." (1 mark)
   A. رَأْسِي كَبِيرٌ
   B. أَشْرَبُ الشَّايَ
   C. الْمَوْزُ لَذِيذٌ
   D. آكُلُ الْأَرُزَّ

36. Which sentence means 'I drink milk'? (1 mark)
   A. uhibbu l-khubza
   B. aakulu l-aruzza
   C. as-samaku ladhiidh
   D. ashrabu l-haliiba

37. What does the Arabic sentence أُنَظِّفُ أَسْنَانِي mean? (1 mark)
   A. I wash my face.
   B. My head is big.
   C. I clean my teeth.
   D. My hand is small.

38. What does the Arabic sentence بَيْتِي كَبِيرٌ mean? (1 mark)
   A. My house is big.
   B. In the room there is a bed.
   C. This is my room.
   D. In the kitchen there is a table.

39. What is a paragraph? (1 mark)
   A. A drawing
   B. A group of sentences about one idea
   C. A single letter
   D. One long word

40. Which Arabic sentence means "I like my house." (1 mark)
   A. فِي الْمَطْبَخِ طَاوِلَةٌ
   B. أُحِبُّ بَيْتِي
   C. فِي الْغُرْفَةِ سَرِيرٌ
   D. هَذِهِ غُرْفَتِي

SECTION B — STRUCTURED / SHORT ANSWERS
----
41. Translate into English: alʿabu yawma s-sabt (2 marks)

42. Translate into English: al-jawwu baarid (2 marks)

43. Write three foods and two drinks in Arabic sounds with meanings. (5 marks) (5 marks)

44. Name three rooms of the house in Arabic (English letters) with meanings. (3 marks) (3 marks)

45. Translate into English: shukran li-istimaaʿikum (2 marks)

46. Translate into English: al-ʿasiiru baarid (2 marks)

47. Give three points you would check when you assess a friend's reading. (3 marks) (3 marks)

48. Give two tips for pronouncing Arabic greetings correctly. (2 marks) (2 marks)

49. Explain why we should show respect when we greet people of a different gender or culture. (3 marks) (3 marks)

50. Read these words and write their sounds in English letters with meanings: مَرْحَبًا and شُكْرًا. (4 marks) (4 marks)

51. Translate into English: fii l-matbakhi taawila (2 marks)

52. Translate into English: uhibbu l-ʿasiira (2 marks)

53. Describe a game you can play with a partner to practise the position words. (3 marks) (3 marks)

54. Translate into English: al-maa'u mufiid (2 marks)

55. Translate into English: ismii Ahmad (2 marks)

56. Translate into English: ash-shamsu haarra (2 marks)

57. Write five words about weather and the environment in Arabic (English letters are fine) with their meanings. (5 marks) (5 marks)

58. Translate into English: al-miftaahu fii l-khizaana (2 marks)

59. Translate into English: asmaʿu bi-udhunii (2 marks)

60. Explain why you should copy sounds carefully when learning Arabic words. (2 marks) (2 marks)

61. Translate into English: nahnu narqusu (2 marks)

62. Read the sentence هَذِهِ أُمِّي and give its meaning. Say which family word it contains. (3 marks) (3 marks)

63. Write a short conversation of three lines in which one friend asks about a party and the other answers. Use English letters. (3 marks) (3 marks)
pages.answers:
ARABIC LANGUAGE — PREMIUM REVISION PAPER #16 · MARKING SCHEME
====

SECTION A
----
1. D — أَنَا
   أَنَا (anaa) means I.

2. C — Thanks to God
   al-hamdu lillaah means 'thanks be to God' and is often said when answering 'How are you?'.

3. A — ismii Ahmad
   ismii means 'my name is', so ismii Ahmad means 'My name is Ahmad'.

4. B — عِنْدِي أَخٌ وَأُخْتٌ
   عِنْدِي أَخٌ وَأُخْتٌ (ʿindii akh wa ukht) means: I have a brother and a sister.

5. C — parents and their children
   The nuclear family is the smallest family group: parents and their children.

6. C — above
   فَوْقَ (fawqa) means above.

7. B — al-ahad
   The Arabic week begins with al-ahad, Sunday.

8. A — ijlis
   ijlis means sit down. qif means stand up.

9. A — food
   طَعَامٌ (taʿaam) means food.

10. C — آكُلُ الْخُبْزَ
   آكُلُ الْخُبْزَ (aakulu l-khubza) means: I eat bread.

11. D — samak
   سَمَكٌ is read samak and means fish.

12. D — udhun
   أُذُنٌ is read udhun and means ear.

13. C — How is the weather today?
   كَيْفَ الْجَوُّ الْيَوْمَ؟ (kayfa l-jawwu l-yawm?) means: How is the weather today?

14. A — zahra
   زَهْرَةٌ is read zahra and means flower.

15. A — It falls
   In a statement the voice falls at the end. In a question it rises.

16. A — The letter has no vowel
   A sukuun shows that the consonant is read without a vowel.

17. B — 28
   The Arabic alphabet has 28 letters.

18. A — ti
   تِ is read ti.

19. A — muu
   مُو is read muu.

20. C — bu
   بُ is read bu.

21. C — Taa, the heavy ط
   طَاوِلَةٌ begins with the heavy letter Taa.

22. D — Thursday
   al-khamiis is Thursday, the fifth day, from the word for five.

23. C — السَّبْتُ
   السَّبْتُ (as-sabt) means Saturday.

24. C — مَدْرَسَةٌ
   مَدْرَسَةٌ (madrasa) means school.

25. A — ʿasiir
   عَصِيرٌ is read ʿasiir and means juice.

26. C — لَذِيذٌ
   لَذِيذٌ (ladhiidh) means delicious.

27. C — بَارِدٌ
   بَارِدٌ (baarid) means cold.

28. B — And the rain is from the sky.
   وَالْمَطَرُ مِنَ السَّمَاءِ (wal-maTaru mina s-samaa'i) means: And the rain is from the sky.

29. A — ن (nuun)
   The word nuur (نُور) starts with nuun.

30. A — Haa
   The letter ح is called Haa.

31. B — cupboard
   خِزَانَةٌ (khizaana) means cupboard.

32. C — The friends eat the cake.
   الْأَصْدِقَاءُ يَأْكُلُونَ الْكَعْكَةَ (al-asdiqaa'u ya'kuluuna l-kaʿka) means: The friends eat the cake.

33. D — We dance.
   نَحْنُ نَرْقُصُ (nahnu narqusu) means: We dance.

34. A — حَلِيبٌ
   حَلِيبٌ (haliib) means milk.

35. D — آكُلُ الْأَرُزَّ
   آكُلُ الْأَرُزَّ (aakulu l-aruzza) means: I eat rice.

36. D — ashrabu l-haliiba
   ashrabu means I drink and haliib means milk.

37. C — I clean my teeth.
   أُنَظِّفُ أَسْنَانِي (unadhdhifu asnaanii) means: I clean my teeth.

38. A — My house is big.
   بَيْتِي كَبِيرٌ (baytii kabiir) means: My house is big.

39. B — A group of sentences about one idea
   A paragraph is a group of related sentences about one idea.

40. B — أُحِبُّ بَيْتِي
   أُحِبُّ بَيْتِي (uhibbu baytii) means: I like my house.

SECTION B
----
41. (2 marks)
   Answer: I play on Saturday.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for the subject or first part and 1 mark for the rest of the meaning.

42. (2 marks)
   Answer: The weather is cold.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for the subject or first part and 1 mark for the rest of the meaning.

43. (5 marks)
   Answer: For example khubz (bread), samak (fish), mawz (bananas), maa' (water), haliib (milk).
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each correct word with meaning.

44. (3 marks)
   Answer: For example ghurfa (room), matbakh (kitchen), hammaam (bathroom), hadiiqa (garden).
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each correct word with meaning, up to 3.

45. (2 marks)
   Answer: Thank you for listening.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for the subject or first part and 1 mark for the rest of the meaning.

46. (2 marks)
   Answer: The juice is cold.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for the subject or first part and 1 mark for the rest of the meaning.

47. (3 marks)
   Answer: Words pronounced correctly; smooth reading without stops; heavy and throat sounds clear; no word skipped.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each valid point.

48. (2 marks)
   Answer: Listen to the teacher first and copy; say long vowels for longer than short vowels; practise the throat sounds kh and ʿ.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each sensible tip.

49. (3 marks)
   Answer: Greeting customs can differ. Using polite words and a smile shows respect. Respect helps boys and girls, men and women to be treated equally and to live peacefully.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for customs differ, 1 mark for polite words, 1 mark for equality or peace.

50. (4 marks)
   Answer: mar-ha-ban (hello) and shuk-ran (thank you).
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each correct reading and 1 mark for each meaning.

51. (2 marks)
   Answer: In the kitchen there is a table.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for the subject or first part and 1 mark for the rest of the meaning.

52. (2 marks)
   Answer: I like juice.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for the subject or first part and 1 mark for the rest of the meaning.

53. (3 marks)
   Answer: Hide a small object. One learner asks ayna l-qalam? The other answers with a sentence such as al-qalamu taHta l-kursii. Then swap.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for hiding an object, 1 mark for the question and 1 mark for the answer sentence.

54. (2 marks)
   Answer: Water is useful (good for you).
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for the subject or first part and 1 mark for the rest of the meaning.

55. (2 marks)
   Answer: My name is Ahmad.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for the subject or first part and 1 mark for the rest of the meaning.

56. (2 marks)
   Answer: The sun is hot.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for the subject or first part and 1 mark for the rest of the meaning.

57. (5 marks)
   Answer: For example shams (sun), sahaab (clouds), matar (rain), riih (wind), samaa' (sky).
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each correct word with its meaning.

58. (2 marks)
   Answer: The key is in the cupboard.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for the subject or first part and 1 mark for the rest of the meaning.

59. (2 marks)
   Answer: I hear with my ear.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for the subject or first part and 1 mark for the rest of the meaning.

60. (2 marks)
   Answer: A small change in a sound can change the meaning, and careful copying makes you clear to the listener.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for change of meaning and 1 mark for being understood.

61. (2 marks)
   Answer: We dance.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for the subject or first part and 1 mark for the rest of the meaning.

62. (3 marks)
   Answer: haadhihi ummii. This is my mother. It contains umm (mother).
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for reading, 1 mark for meaning and 1 mark for the family word.

63. (3 marks)
   Answer: A: hal ʿindaka hafla? B: naʿam, ʿindii hafla. A: mabruuk!
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for the question, 1 mark for the answer and 1 mark for a suitable closing wish.
